text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.73% today to close at $147.01, continuing a sharp two-week rally of over 13%. The stock has benefited from a sustained surge in global oil prices—Brent crude topped $109 this week after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian facilities, and world oil prices are now trading at $115.22 per barrel. For a major oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices flow directly to the bottom line, which is why the stock has climbed steadily since mid-October even as U.S. oil prices sit lower at $107.89.

The broader geopolitical picture has tightened energy markets over the past week. Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian diesel facilities have disrupted global fuel supplies (particularly diesel), and escalating attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz add to supply concerns—both factors that typically support crude prices where oil producers generate their profits.
